campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 6, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council's agenda for October 6, 2026, lists discussion of temporary legal services while the city transitions to a new city attorney, along with compensation and working conditions for certain unrepresented city employees. The agenda also includes a proposed market adjustment to the city manager's salary.
keyTopics: Temporary legal services arrangement during the city attorney transition
Compensation and working conditions for unrepresented confidential, classified management, and unclassified management employees
Proposed market adjustment to the city manager's salary

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 7, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council's October 7, 2026, agenda listed routine items like meeting minutes, check registers, and the Treasurer's Report, alongside several notable policy decisions. Key items include a $2.5 million budget amendment for the Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation, a decision on the City's long-term law enforcement provider, and a review of animal care service options. The agenda also included a public hearing on annual updates to the City Code.
keyTopics: Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation Project budget amendment for $2,500,000
Decision on long-term law enforcement provider, including possible agreement with Los Gatos Monte Sereno Police Department
Comparison of animal care service providers, including whether to continue with San Jose Animal Care and Services
No Parking Anytime zone proposed for a section of Chester Avenue near Arcadia Palms Drive
Public hearing on annual City Code updates covering appeals scheduling and City Commissioner qualifications

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 13, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the Los Altos City Council meeting of October 13, 2026, lists routine financial reports, several resolutions for city infrastructure and housing programs, and a discussion of the Commission and Committee Handbook. Items include sewer and street repair project acceptances, a residential electrification rebate budget appropriation, and updated Below Market Rate housing guidelines.
keyTopics: Resolution adopting an updated Conflict of Interest Code for staff and commissioners
Resolutions accepting completion of sanitary sewer spot repair and annual street repaving projects
Resolution appropriating $78,000 for a residential electrification rebate program
Resolution approving updated Below Market Rate For-Sale and Rental Housing Guidelines, found exempt from CEQA review
Discussion of the Commission and Committee Handbook and possible revisions

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 6, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council's October 6, 2026, agenda listed routine business, including approval of minutes from two prior meetings, a financial accounts and payroll report, and a review of the July 2026 revenue and expenditure reports. It also included a contract-related item involving a tree services bidder, an amendment to an existing agreement, an updated work plan from the Finance Commission, and a resolution to amend the Town's purchasing policy.
keyTopics: Relieving Denali Tree Services of its bid due to a bidder's mistake
First Amendment to an existing agreement authorized for execution by the Town Manager
Finance Commission's updated 2026 Work Plan
Resolution amending the Town of Los Gatos Purchasing Policy (Policy 4-06)
July 2026 Expenditure and Revenue Reports

san-jose.title: San José City Council — October 13, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda listed three briefing items for San José's City Council on preparing for the upcoming rainy season and ongoing water infrastructure projects. Topics include flood and storm readiness, a major dam retrofit and creek flood protection effort, and a project to turn wastewater into clean drinking water.
keyTopics: Joint update on El Niño and flood/storm preparedness for the 2026-2027 rainy season
Status update on the Anderson Dam Seismic Retrofit Project and Coyote Creek Flood Protection Project
Status update on the Pure Water Silicon Valley Potable Reuse Project

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — October 13, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council's October 13, 2026, agenda includes several proclamations, a Caltrain presentation, and a second reading of a historic preservation ordinance. Other listed items cover ambulance billing fees, a citywide fiber network concept, a development agreement amendment for the LinkedIn campus, an interim ordinance on detention facilities, and a proposed solar and battery energy storage contract.
keyTopics: Historic Preservation Ordinance and Zoning Map Amendment (Second Reading)
Conceptual Design for a Citywide Fiber Network
LinkedIn Development Agreement Amendment at East Middlefield Road and Maude Avenue
Interim Urgency Ordinance for Detention or Custodial Facilities
Energy Services Contract for Solar Photovoltaic Systems and Battery Energy Storage Project

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council agenda for October 6, 2026, includes several recognitions, such as local Little League All-Stars and Indigenous Peoples' Day, along with routine approvals like meeting minutes and bill payments. The agenda also lists public hearings on water conservation rules for nonfunctional turf, a possible service worker retention ordinance, and public art for the Lakewood Park renovation.
keyTopics: Recognition of 2026 Sunnyvale Little League Junior Division All-Stars, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Friends of the Library Week, and Sunnyvale Stands United Against Hate Week
Proposed ordinance amendment to implement AB 1572, prohibiting potable water use for nonfunctional turf irrigation, found exempt under CEQA Guidelines Section 15307
Discussion and possible introduction of a Service Worker Retention Ordinance
Approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation
Amendment to increase funding and extend a contract with WSP USA Inc. for environmental consulting at the SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill

cupertino.title: Cupertino Administrative Hearing — October 8, 2026
cupertino.summary: This Cupertino Administrative Hearing agenda covers approval of prior meeting minutes and one land-use application: a proposal to split a 32,691-square-foot lot on McClellan Road into three separate residential lots. No old or new business items beyond this were listed.
keyTopics: Approval of the July 16, 2026, Administrative Hearing minutes
Parcel Map Application (TM-2025-010) to subdivide a lot at 22181 McClellan Road into three lots (10,572, 10,930, and 11,189 square feet) in the R1-32.5 zoning district

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — October 6, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council's agenda for October 6, 2026, includes a report and possible Council action on pedestrian access restrictions along parts of Lawrence and San Tomas Expressways, plus a staff presentation seeking Council input on updating city policies for new data center development, including water use and grid participation. The agenda also lists a joint dinner meeting with the Parks and Recreation Commission and several proclamations.
keyTopics: Report and potential Council action affirming pedestrian access restrictions on portions of Lawrence and San Tomas Expressways
Staff presentation on updating city policies for new data center development, including water usage and demand-side grid support participation
Joint dinner meeting with the Parks and Recreation Commission
Proclamations for Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Domestic Violence Awareness Month, and United Against Hate Week

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council's September 15, 2026, agenda listed items on housing and community development funding, a red light camera traffic safety program, the condition of the Milpitas Community Center, and bond refunding actions tied to the former Redevelopment Agency's Successor Agency. The agenda does not confirm which items were actually discussed or decided.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan approval
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution and bond sale/issuance for refunding bonds tied to the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Human Relations Commission Meeting — October 8, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda for this Palo Alto Human Relations Commission meeting listed three items: setting the 2027 City Council meeting schedule and reviewing citywide dates of significance, prioritizing housing and human services funding needs for FY 2028, and examining fee stabilization and affordability protections for below-market-rate homeowners in HOAs. The agenda allotted specific time blocks for each topic.
keyTopics: Proposed 2027 City Council meeting schedule and citywide dates of significance list
Priority-setting for FY 2028 Human Services Resource Allocation Process (HSRAP) funding
HOA fee stabilization and affordability protections for below-market-rate homeowners
